description: The figure contains two stacked line plots illustrating piecewise linear “sawtooth” sequences as a function of \(m\), with a vertical dashed reference at \(m_0\) in both plots. In both plots, the x-axis is labeled \(m\), uses a linear scale, starts at 0 at the origin, and extends rightward past the marked position \(m_0\); there are no numeric tick labels shown. In the top plot, the y-axis is labeled \(n\), uses a linear scale with the origin labeled 0, and includes three horizontal dashed reference levels labeled \(w\), \(c-a-s\), and \(c-a\). A single black solid line without markers forms repeated ramps that rise linearly from near the baseline to a peak aligned with the \(c-a\) dashed level, then drop sharply to a lower value and repeat; to the right of \(m_0\), the same sawtooth pattern continues with visibly smaller peak heights than the earlier peaks, with peaks staying below the \(c-a\) level and oscillating around the \(c-a-s\) level. In the bottom plot, the y-axis is labeled \(a\), uses a linear scale with the origin labeled 0, and includes two horizontal dashed reference levels labeled \(c\) and \(w+a+s\). A single black solid line without markers again forms a repeating sawtooth: it rises linearly from 0 up to a peak aligned with the \(c\) dashed level, then drops sharply and repeats; after the vertical dashed line at \(m_0\), the sawtooth continues with peaks that remain below \(c\) and oscillate around the \(w+a+s\) dashed level.
